Editorial selection

Best philosophy quotes

Not a ranking by popularity alone. These passages were chosen for clarity, argumentative bite, and lasting use in teaching and reflection.

  1. The unexamined life is not worth living for a human being.
    Socrates
    Self-examination
  2. What I do not know, I do not claim to know.
    Socrates
    Knowledge
  3. It is worse to do injustice than to suffer it.
    Socrates
    Justice
  4. Justice is doing one's own work and not meddling in others'.
    Plato
    Justice
  5. Let us not become haters of argument — that is a great danger to the soul.
    Plato
    Reason
  6. Extreme freedom seems to change into nothing but extreme slavery.
    Plato
    Freedom
  7. The human good is activity of soul in accordance with virtue.
    Aristotle
    Happiness
  8. Virtues arise in us neither by nature nor contrary to nature; we are fitted by nature to receive them, and are brought to completion by habit.
    Aristotle
    Habit
  9. Virtue is a state concerned with choice, lying in a mean relative to us.
    Aristotle
    Meaning
  10. Death is nothing to us: for what has been dissolved has no sensation, and what has no sensation is nothing to us.
    Epicurus
    Death
  11. Pleasure is the beginning and end of the happy life — not the pleasures of profligates, but freedom from pain in the body and from disturbance in the soul.
    Epicurus
    Life
  12. Of all that wisdom provides for the happiness of a whole life, by far the greatest is the possession of friendship.
    Epicurus
    Friendship
  13. Of things, some are in our power, and some are not.
    Epictetus
    Philosophy
  14. It is not things that disturb people, but their judgments about things.
    Epictetus
    Judgment
  15. It is not because things are difficult that we do not dare; it is because we do not dare that they are difficult.
    Seneca
    Courage
  16. Fate leads the willing and drags the unwilling.
    Seneca
    Fate
  17. There is no easy way from the earth to the stars.
    Seneca
    Philosophy
  18. Leisure without study is death — a tomb for a living man.
    Seneca
    Learning
  19. He who has learned how to die has unlearned how to be a slave.
    Seneca
    Death
  20. The universe is change; life is opinion.
    Marcus Aurelius
    Change
  21. Begin the morning by saying to yourself: Today I shall meet the busybody, the ungrateful, the arrogant…
    Marcus Aurelius
    Philosophy
  22. Do not act as if you were going to live ten thousand years. Death hangs over you. While you live, while it is in your power, be good.
    Marcus Aurelius
    Philosophy
  23. If you are distressed by anything external, it is not the thing itself that disturbs you, but your own judgment about it.
    Marcus Aurelius
    Judgment
  24. What then is time? If no one asks me, I know; if I wish to explain it to one who asks, I do not know.
    Augustine of Hippo
    Time
  25. The greatest thing in the world is to know how to belong to oneself.
    Michel de Montaigne
    Autonomy
  26. Once in a lifetime, everything must be doubted.
    René Descartes
    Knowledge
  27. A free man thinks of nothing less than of death; and his wisdom is a meditation not on death but on life.
    Baruch Spinoza
    Freedom
  28. Man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains.
    Jean-Jacques Rousseau
    Freedom
  29. Dare to know! Have the courage to use your own understanding!
    Immanuel Kant
    Enlightenment
  30. Man is something that shall be overcome.
    Friedrich Nietzsche
    Philosophy
  31. Despair is the sickness unto death — the self's refusal to be itself.
    Søren Kierkegaard
    Self
  32. Trust thyself: every heart vibrates to that iron string.
    Ralph Waldo Emerson
    Self
  33. The mass of men lead lives of quiet desperation.
    Henry David Thoreau
    Awakening
  34. Education is not preparation for life; education is life itself.
    John Dewey
    Education
  35. It is better to be a human being dissatisfied than a pig satisfied; better to be Socrates dissatisfied than a fool satisfied.
    John Stuart Mill
    Happiness
  36. There is but one truly serious philosophical problem, and that is suicide.
    Albert Camus
    Meaning
  37. One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman.
    Simone de Beauvoir
    Self
  38. Virtue does not come from money, but from virtue come money and all other good things for human beings.
    Socrates
    Virtue
  39. It is impossible to think of anything at all in the world, or indeed even beyond it, that could be considered good without limitation except a good will.
    Immanuel Kant
    Freedom
  40. To will oneself free is also to will others free.
    Simone de Beauvoir
    Freedom
  41. Believe that life is worth living, and your belief will help create the fact.
    William James
    Knowledge
  42. A foolish consistency is the hobgoblin of little minds.
    Ralph Waldo Emerson
    Authenticity
  43. The usefulness of living is not in length of days, but in their use: one may have lived long, and yet have lived little.
    Michel de Montaigne
    Life
  44. To know, in order to foresee, so as to be able to act.
    Auguste Comte
    Knowledge
  45. Solitude is the lot of all outstanding minds.
    Arthur Schopenhauer
    Philosophy
  46. Despair is not to will to be oneself — or else to will to be oneself.
    Søren Kierkegaard
    Philosophy
  47. Fear is the main source of superstition, and one of the main sources of cruelty. To conquer fear is the beginning of wisdom.
    Bertrand Russell
    Fear
  48. We feel that even if all possible scientific questions are answered, the problems of life have still not been touched at all.
    Ludwig Wittgenstein
    Science
